title: Direct image from an open and closed section
statement:
Let $p:V\to X$ be a scheme morphism and
$s:X\hookrightarrow V$ an
open immersion with
closed image and $p s=\operatorname{id}_X$.
For a finite ring $\Lambda$ and
$K\in\hyperref[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]{D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)}$,
restriction to this component gives a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rp_*s_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}K,
$$

where $Rp_*$ and $s_!$ are the
derived direct image and
extension by zero.

proof.text: Use the already proved source theorem Etale.isIso_openImmersionLowerShriekToLowerStar_of_isClosed_range to identify J=s_! with R=s_*. This is the clopen gluing and component argument already implemented in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.LowerShriek.Proper; it is valid directly for module coefficients. Transfer preservation of finite colimits from J to R along this natural isomorphism. Since R is a right adjoint it also preserves finite limits, so R is exact.

Let adj be s^* adjoint to s_*. Its counit is invertible since pushforward along an open immersion is fully faithful. Prove that the derived counit is invertible: on Qh(N), the factorization Adjunction.derivedPlus_counit_app_fac expresses it, after precomposing with the invertible image of the right-derived comparison, as the localization of the homotopy-category counit composed with an exact-functor comparison. The homotopy-category counit is invertible because the induced right adjoint is fully faithful. Exactness of R makes its right-derived comparison invertible. Finally every bounded-below derived object is isomorphic to Qh(N), and naturality transports invertibility. This is the private proved helper exact_derived_counit_isIso.

Consequently Rs_* is fully faithful. Exactness and the clopen comparison give an isomorphism D(s_!) = D(s_*) isomorphic to Rs_*. For each K, D(s_!)(K) lies in the essential image of Rs_*, so the unit of Ds^* adjoint to Rs_* is invertible on D(s_!)(K), by Adjunction.isIso_unit_app_of_iso.

The exact left adjoint s^* implies s_* preserves injective objects. Apply Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompIso' to lowerStarComp for s,p and ps=id, and then lowerStarIdDerivedPlus. This gives c: Rs_* followed by Rp_* isomorphic to identity. Whisker the derived unit of step 3 by Rp_*, and compose with c evaluated on Ds^*D(s_!)(K), to obtain a natural isomorphism t: Rp_*D(s_!) isomorphic to Ds^*D(s_!).

The unit of s_! adjoint to s^* is invertible. Applying the exact derived functor and the identity/composition comparison isomorphisms gives a: identity isomorphic to Ds^*D(s_!). Define e=t followed by a inverse. Then e followed by a is t by cancellation of a inverse with a. Expanding t is exactly the displayed canonical-map equation; the construction from natural transformations already supplies naturality and independence of representatives.
